content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have a question about copying a program from a [product_name] to a program module. If the [product_name] is stopped but powered on, and has no program module inserted, I plan to insert a blank program module into the programmed [product_name]. Then, using the programming menu, I'll select the option to copy from device to card. After the copy finishes, can I remove the program module without turning off the [product_name]? Next, I want to insert this program module with the copied program into another [product_name]. Is this procedure safe? Thanks for your help.

Hello, Honestly, I'm unsure if that's permitted. Why not just power down the device? Since the program is saved in nonvolatile memory, as described in the manual: Note: You do not need a module to back up the circuit program in your [product_name]. The circuit program is automatically stored in nonvolatile memory when you leave programming mode. Best regards, [user_name]

Yes, your method is correct for copying to a memory card. Copying from a memory card to a [product_name] is even easier: - Power off the device - Insert the memory card containing the program - Power on the device - Wait until you see the correct indication on the display - Remove the memory card - Occasionally, you may need to select <START> on the screen, and that's it.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants discuss how to correctly transfer programs between [product_name] devices using program or memory modules. There's uncertainty about whether the process can be done without shutting down the device, with nonvolatile memory highlighted as a safeguard. The discussion covers different approaches and confirms the standard copying procedure.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want a reliable and straightforward method to copy programs between [product_name] devices using program modules, preferably without needing to turn off the equipment.
